target_gates.description: One complete threshold boundary remains anchored in the near-side scene.
Near and far spaces are simultaneously visible and materially distinct.
A crossing subject or object intersects the plane with coherent occlusion.
The physical effect changes locally at the threshold rather than across the whole frame.
A glowing ring, mirror, window, or empty arch does not substitute for the two-world crossing relation.
One complete constructed body reads as a single agent.
Material remains continuous across torso, limbs, and joints.
Seams, fitted blocks, packed clay, or bindings show deliberate assembly.
Grounded motion and one object interaction demonstrate independent agency.
A statue, costume, robot, rubble pile, or inscription alone does not substitute.
